patients.summary: Healthy young woman, a student then graduate student on a parent's plan, with the practice since 2017. Her chart is a run of sexually transmitted infections seen mostly at an outside gynecology office and an emergency department: early syphilis, chlamydial cervicitis, primary genital herpes and three episodes of disseminated gonococcal infection, with outside records that arrive late or not at all.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 20 y/o college student home in Greenfield for the rest of the summer. A family member suggested the practice; she has not had a regular doctor since aging out of her pediatrician. Membership packet emailed. New patient visit booked 8/22 at 10:00. Asked her to bring her insurance card (she is on a parent's plan) and any vaccine paperwork she can find.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

Leah is 20 and starting her junior year at college in the fall. Comes in to set up primary care now that she is too old for her pediatric office. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations. No surgeries.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Gyn: menarche at 12, cycles regular about every 28 days. Never pregnant. Has not had a pelvic exam or Pap yet.
Family: mother has hypothyroidism; father has high blood pressure. No other family history she knows of.
Social: full-time student, lives with her parents in Greenfield between semesters. Never smoked. Drinks socially, 1-2 drinks most weeks. No drug use.

ROS: negative across systems.

Exam: well-appearing young woman. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin clear. No lymphadenopathy.

A/P
1. Health maintenance, age 20. Healthy. Pap due at 21; will do it at next year's physical. Asked her to have her pediatric office send the immunization record so we can see where the HPV and meningococcal series landed. Flu shot when it arrives this fall.
2. Counseled on safer sex and contraception options; she is not currently sexually active and would like to revisit it later.

Return in one year, sooner as needed.

Childhood primary series complete per state schedule. MMR x2 (1997, 2001). Varicella x2 (1997, 2001). Tdap 10/2008. MenACWY 10/2008 with booster 8/2013. HPV quadrivalent 3-dose series completed 4/2009.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Now 22, senior year. Doing well, busy with a thesis. Became sexually active this past year, one partner at a time, condoms most of the time. No pelvic pain, discharge or sores. Periods regular. No meds.

Social: no tobacco. Alcohol a couple of drinks a week at most.
Family: unchanged (mother hypothyroid, father hypertension).

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Thyroid normal. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix without lesions, scant normal physiologic secretions. Bimanual without tenderness or masses. Pap and swab collected.

A/P
1. Preventive care. First Pap today. Gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT, HIV and hepatitis C screening sent as routine for her age. Basic labs.
2. Contraception: content with condoms for now; reviewed that the pill, ring, implant and IUD are all options whenever she wants to talk about them.
3. Flu vaccine declined today, says she will get it on campus.

One year.

documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Your physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Leah, everything from your physical came back normal: the Pap, the infection screening and the blood work. Next Pap would be due in three years. Have a good semester.

No meds. NKDA. Never smoker. Social drinker.

OUTSIDE OB/GYN OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 04/27/2020
Copy to primary care physician

Reason for visit: well-woman exam; contraception and STI prevention counseling.

23 y/o G0, graduate student, here for a routine gynecologic exam. She has recently begun a new relationship and wants to go over birth control and how to protect herself from infections, and asks whether she should be tested. No symptoms today. Cycles regular. LMP about two weeks ago. Denies any genital sores, abnormal discharge or burning with urination.

PMH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother - hypothyroidism; father - hypertension.
SH: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks/week; graduate student.

Vitals: within normal limits.
Pelvic: external genitalia normal. Speculum: cervix without mucopurulent discharge. Bimanual normal; no cervical motion tenderness; no adnexal masses or tenderness.

Labs: RPR nonreactive. Gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT negative.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Well-woman exam, normal.
2. Contraception counseling: reviewed combined pills, progestin-only options, the implant, copper and hormonal IUDs. She prefers to rely on condoms for now and will call if she wants to start a method.
3. STI prevention: syphilis screen negative, GC/CT negative. Encouraged consistent condom use with new partners.
Return as needed or in one year.

documents.title: Gynecology Office Visit (outside)
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 07/29/2020
Sent in response to records request

CC: vaginal discharge.

Seen about three months after her well visit. For several months she has noticed a white discharge. No odor. No itching, burning or irritation. LMP began 14 days ago; cycles every 28 days. One partner; condoms not every time.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Vitals normal.
Speculum: small amount of white mucoid discharge at the cervical os. No erythema. No lesions. No sign of trauma.

Wet mount: numerous epithelial cells; rare PMNs; normal vaginal flora (lactobacilli predominant); no trichomonads; no clue cells. pH 4.5.

Impression: physiologic leukorrhea. No evidence of bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis or yeast.
Plan: reassured; no treatment needed. Reviewed what normal mid-cycle discharge looks like and when to come back (odor, itching, color change, pelvic pain).

We never got the July note; requesting it.

No meds. NKDA. No tobacco. Light alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Pelvic deferred, followed by gyn.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap next due 2021. Flu vaccine given.
2. Gyn care outside; records request sent for 7/29 visit.
3. Mood good, PHQ-2 of 1.

Year.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN DOCUMENTATION
Visit: 10/22/2021

Chief complaint: fever, malaise, rash x 2 weeks.

HPI: 25 y/o F. About two weeks of low energy, feeling feverish, and a rash that started on her chest and back and has spread down her arms and legs, now on her palms and the soles of her feet. Not itchy. When asked, she recalls a few painless sores in the genital area some months back that went away without treatment; she never had them checked. Last syphilis test she knows of was negative at a gyn visit about a year and a half ago. Several recent partners, condoms inconsistently.

PMH: none active. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother hypothyroidism, father hypertension.

Exam: VS within normal limits. Diffuse nonpruritic maculopapular eruption over trunk and extremities including palms and soles. Generalized lymphadenopathy with palpable epitrochlear nodes bilaterally. Oropharynx clear. No meningismus. Neuro nonfocal; no visual complaints.

Results: RPR reactive, 1:64. TP-PA reactive. HIV Ag/Ab nonreactive.

ED course / MDM: presentation and serologies consistent with early (secondary) syphilis. No neurologic or ocular symptoms. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM given x1; observed 30 min, no reaction. Counseled on possible fever/myalgias in the first day after treatment. Health department partner services referral made. Abstain until rash resolved and partners treated.

Dx: Early syphilis, secondary.
Dispo: home. Follow up with PCP within 1-2 weeks; repeat RPR at 6 and 12 months.

documents.title: ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I went to the ER last night for the rash I've had. They said it's syphilis and gave me a shot of penicillin in the hip. I feel kind of achy today but they warned me about that. They told me to see you in a week or two. Can I get an appointment? Kind of freaked out honestly.

documents.title: RE: ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and I'm glad you went in. This is very treatable and the shot you got is the right treatment. The achiness the first day is expected; acetaminophen is fine. Our front desk will reach out Monday to book you for next week. If you get a headache that won't quit, vision changes, or anything that scares you, call the after-hours line.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
FOLLOW-UP AFTER ED VISIT

Seen 10/22 at the regional ED (record received 10/27 and reviewed): two weeks of malaise and a rash on trunk, limbs, palms and soles; remote painless genital sores; RPR 1:64, TP-PA reactive, HIV negative. Treated with benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM once.

Since then: achy and warm for about a day after the shot, then better. Rash is fading and mostly gone from her hands. Energy coming back. Health department called her about partners; she gave them names.

Sexual history: several partners over the past year, condoms inconsistently. We talked about it plainly; she is not interested in a lecture and I did not give one.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. A few faint coppery macules on forearms; palms and soles nearly clear. Small shotty nodes in the neck and groin. No mucosal lesions seen.

A/P
1. Early syphilis, treated. Repeat RPR at 6 months (late April) and 12 months (October with her physical). Expect a fourfold drop by 6-12 months. Avoid sex until rash gone and partners treated.
2. High-risk sexual behavior: multiple partners, inconsistent condoms. Condoms with each partner; regular testing here.
3. Old 'syphilis screening negative' entry from April 2020 closed out.

RPR order placed for April.

documents.title: RPR 6 months
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: RPR 1:8, down from 1:64 at diagnosis in October. That is better than a fourfold fall; appropriate response to treatment. Repeat at 12 months with her physical.

documents.title: Your syphilis follow-up test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Leah, good news. Your RPR has come down from 1:64 to 1:8, which is exactly the drop we want after treatment. One more check in the fall when you come in for your physical.

documents.title: RE: Your syphilis follow-up test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Oh thank god. OK see you in the fall.

26 now, third year of grad school. Feels well. No rash, sores or discharge. Partners: still more than one; condoms 'more than before.'

No meds. NKDA. Never smoker. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a week.

Exam: vitals as charted. Skin clear, no residual rash on palms or soles. No adenopathy. Heart, lungs, abdomen normal.

A/P
1. Early syphilis, treated 10/2021: 12-month RPR drawn today.
2. High-risk sexual behavior: reviewed condoms and testing every 3-6 months while she has multiple partners.
3. Pap done 2021; next 2024.
4. Flu and bivalent COVID booster today, opposite arms.

Physical next October.

documents.title: RPR 12 months
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: RPR 1:2. Sustained decline from 1:64; serologic response adequate. Early syphilis marked resolved. A low titer may persist. Patient notified through portal.

documents.title: Gynecology Office Visit (outside)
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 11/01/2022
Faxed per request 1/2023

CC: burning with urination, discharge.

26 y/o G0 with a history of an ED evaluation for genital sores and our prior visits. Three days of dysuria, going more often, and a yellow vaginal discharge. Denies fever, flank or back pain, abdominal pain. LMP 2 weeks ago, normal. Multiple partners; condoms used inconsistently.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Vitals within normal limits.
Pelvic: mucopurulent discharge from the cervical os; cervical motion tenderness present.

Urine hCG negative. UA: no bacteria, no WBCs.
CT/GC NAAT: chlamydia DETECTED; gonorrhea not detected (resulted 11/3, patient informed by phone).

A/P: Chlamydia trachomatis cervicitis.
- Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 7 days, started at visit.
- Abstain 7 days after completing treatment and until partners treated; expedited partner therapy offered.
- Retest in 3 months.

documents.title: Outside prescription fill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Medication history refresh shows doxycycline hyclate 100 mg caps, #14, filled 11/1/22, prescriber at an outside OB/GYN office. No note from that office on file for this. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: FYI
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just so you know, I saw my gyn on Tuesday because it was burning when I peed and I had some discharge. They called yesterday and it was chlamydia. I'm on doxycycline twice a day for a week. Ugh. Do I need to do anything on your end?

documents.title: RE: FYI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, Leah. Doxycycline for a week is the right treatment. Take it with a full glass of water and stay upright for a while after, and go easy on direct sun. No sex until a week after you finish and your partners have been treated. We should retest in about 3 months; I'll have the staff set that up for early February. I'll also ask your gyn's office for the visit note.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Nothing received yet from the outside OB/GYN office for the 11/1/22 visit. Called their records line, re-sent the release by fax. They said 2-3 weeks.

documents.title: Retest swab
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for 3-month test of reinfection after chlamydia treated in November. Finished all 7 days of doxycycline. No symptoms. Self-collected vaginal swab for CT/GC NAAT, instructions given. Results to portal.

documents.title: Retest negative
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Leah, your repeat swab was negative for both chlamydia and gonorrhea. You are all clear from the November infection. Keep the condoms going.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 10 days

documents.title: Patient call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Went to the ED Saturday with painful blisters 'down there', burning with urination, fever and feeling run down; started about a week after sex with someone new. ED told her it looked like herpes, swabbed it, and started valacyclovir. She got a call Sunday that the swab was positive for herpes. Still sore, urinating is painful but she is managing; using sitz baths. Fever gone since yesterday. Able to urinate. Wants to be seen. Booked with PCP Thursday 5/4. Told to call back if she cannot pass urine, gets a headache with stiff neck, or the pain gets worse.

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
FOLLOW-UP, GENITAL HERPES

No ED record yet; history from Leah and the fill history.

About a week after unprotected sex with a new partner she developed fever and malaise, then three days of painful urination and blisters on the labia. Seen in the ED Saturday 4/29. She says they examined her, noted swollen glands in both groins, checked her urine, swabbed a sore, and started valacyclovir 1 g twice a day for 10 days. The ED called her Sunday: swab positive for herpes simplex. She does not know the type. Day 6 of valacyclovir, taking it on schedule. Fever gone. Urination still stings but is better.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Labia with several shallow healing ulcers, no new vesicles. Tender, mobile inguinal nodes on both sides. No vaginal discharge on inspection.

A/P
1. Primary genital HSV infection, healing on valacyclovir. Finish the 10 days. Sitz baths; urinating in a warm bath helps the stinging. Talked through what recurrences look like and that they tend to be milder. Disclosure to partners, condoms, no sex during sores.
2. High-risk sexual behavior: repeat STI here at any time she wants testing.
3. Requesting ED record.

documents.title: ED records follow-up

2. High-risk sexual behavior, history of syphilis and chlamydia: condoms; testing any time.
3. Pap due next year.
4. Flu and updated COVID vaccine today. Basic chemistry panel sent.

See her next fall.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE - outside facility
DOS 04/27/2024

CC: joint pain moving from joint to joint, fever, rash.

HPI: 27F with prior STIs (early syphilis 2021, chlamydial cervicitis 2022, primary genital HSV 2023). Two days of pain and swelling that shifts between joints, now mostly wrists and knees, with fevers and chills. Rash started as small red spots on arms and legs and turned into little pus-topped blisters. Multiple partners, barrier protection inconsistent.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Triage: T 38.7 C, HR 102, BP 120/78.
Exam: uncomfortable, moderate distress with pain. Wrists and knees swollen and tender; pain along the flexor tendon sheaths of both wrists, consistent with tenosynovitis. Scattered small vesiculopustules on the extremities, a few with an erythematous halo. Heart tachycardic, regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Results: WBC 15.0 (80% neutrophils). CRP 90 mg/L. ESR 70 mm/hr. UA unremarkable. Gram stain of unroofed pustule: gram-negative diplococci.

MDM: arthritis-dermatitis syndrome; picture is disseminated gonococcal infection. Blood cultures x2, cervical and pharyngeal swabs sent. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given. Admit to medicine.

Dx: disseminated gonococcal infection.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily to complete 7 days of therapy (last dose 5/3)

results.text: Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolated; susceptible to ceftriaxone and cefixime

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/27/2024 - Discharged 04/30/2024

Principal diagnosis: disseminated gonococcal infection (arthritis-dermatitis).

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED with fever, migratory polyarthralgia with wrist tenosynovitis, and vesiculopustular skin lesions; Gram stain of a lesion showed gram-negative diplococci. Started ceftriaxone 1 g IV every 24 hours. Cervical NAAT positive for N. gonorrhoeae, negative for chlamydia. Cervical culture grew N. gonorrhoeae susceptible to ceftriaxone and cefixime. Blood cultures without growth. Fever resolved within 36 hours; joint swelling and skin lesions improving. No effusion requiring aspiration.

Discharge meds: cefixime 400 mg PO BID to finish a 7-day total course (through 5/3).
Allergies: NKDA.
Condition at discharge: stable, afebrile, ambulating.
Instructions: no sex until treatment complete and partners treated; partner services notified. PCP follow-up within 1 week.

Follow-up: primary care.

documents.title: in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm in the hospital since Saturday. My joints blew up and I had a fever and spots, they're saying it's gonorrhea that spread into my blood/joints. On IV antibiotics. Feeling better today. They said I need to see you after I get out, probably Tuesday or Wednesday?

documents.title: RE: in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you're going through this, Leah, and glad you're improving. I'll have the front desk hold a spot for you next Tuesday 5/7. Bring your discharge paperwork.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT

Admitted 4/27-4/30 for disseminated gonococcal infection (ED note and discharge summary received 5/3, reviewed): fever, migratory joint pain with wrist tenosynovitis, pustular rash; WBC 15.0, CRP 90, ESR 70; lesion Gram stain GN diplococci; cervical NAAT and culture positive for gonorrhea, susceptible; blood cultures negative. Ceftriaxone IV, then cefixime to finish 7 days.

Today: finished the cefixime Friday. No fever. Wrists still a little stiff in the morning, knees fine. Spots have crusted and are fading.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Wrists without swelling, full range. Knees without effusion. A few small crusted macules on forearms and shins.

A/P
1. Disseminated gonococcal infection, treated and clinically resolved. Call for fever, a hot swollen joint, or new spots.
2. High-risk sexual behavior. Long talk about condoms with every partner. Partners treated per health department.
3. Med rec: no ongoing medications.

Dx: disseminated gonococcal infection, recurrent.

documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 05/07/2025 - Discharge 05/10/2025

Diagnosis: recurrent disseminated gonococcal infection with right knee gonococcal arthritis.

Course: Second episode in about a year. Right knee aspirate in the ED: 50,000 WBC, 90% PMNs, gram-negative diplococci; culture grew N. gonorrhoeae, susceptible to ceftriaxone and cefixime. Cervical NAAT positive for gonorrhea; chlamydia negative; pharyngeal gonorrhea NAAT negative. Blood cultures no growth. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily with rapid defervescence; knee effusion decreased and range of motion improved; no repeat aspiration needed. Rash fading.

Discharge medications: cefixime 400 mg PO BID to complete 7 days total (through 5/13).
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge condition: good.
Follow-up: PCP in one week. Abstain until treatment complete and partners treated.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT

No hospital records yet; she forgot her discharge papers. History from Leah and the fill history.

Admitted 5/7-5/10 at the regional hospital: fever, joint pain moving around, rash on palms and soles, then a hot swollen right knee that was drained in the ED. Told the fluid showed the same gonorrhea bacteria as last year. IV antibiotics, then cefixime twice daily; last dose tomorrow morning.

Today: no fever since Thursday. Right knee still a little stiff going down stairs but much better. Rash fading.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Right knee: no warmth, mild residual swelling, flexion slightly limited. Wrists without swelling. A few faint macules on palms.

A/P
1. Recurrent disseminated gonococcal infection, second episode, on oral step-down. Finish cefixime. Gentle range of motion for the knee. Records requested from the hospital.
2. High-risk sexual behavior. Condoms, partner treatment.

Recheck as needed; physical in the fall.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

29. Well. Right knee has been fine since early summer. No fevers, rashes, sores or discharge. No meds.

Problem list cleanup: the May DGI episode was still showing as active; it was treated and has resolved. Closed.

Exam: vitals as charted. Right knee without effusion, full range. Skin clear. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P
1. History of two DGI episodes (2024, 2025), treated, no residual joint problems.
2. High-risk sexual behavior: condoms; testing any time she wants it.
3. Pap 2024 normal; next 2027.
4. Flu and updated COVID today.

See next fall.

EMERGENCY MEDICINE NOTE (outside)
Service date: 05/02/2026

CC: R knee pain/swelling x2 days.

HPI: 29F, DGI in 2024 and 2025. Two days of a painful, swollen right knee without any injury. Low-grade fevers. Noticed a few small pustules on her palm that do not hurt. No vaginal discharge, no pelvic pain. No medications. NKDA.

VS: T 38.2 C, BP 120/75, HR 88, RR 16.
Exam: right knee warm, swollen and tender, limited flexion and extension due to pain. Palms with a few scattered pustules on a red base. Wrists and other joints without swelling.

Arthrocentesis R knee: WBC 20,000/mm3, 90% PMN. Gram stain: no organisms seen. Culture pending. Blood cultures x2. Cervical NAAT and culture sent.

MDM: third presentation compatible with DGI with knee involvement; negative Gram stain does not exclude it. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV. Admit.

documents.title: Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
05/02/2026 to 05/05/2026

Diagnosis: disseminated gonococcal infection, third episode (prior 2024, 2025), right knee arthritis and palmar pustules.

Course: Right knee aspirate 20,000 WBC with 90% neutrophils, Gram stain negative; synovial culture final no growth. Blood cultures no growth. Cervical NAAT positive for N. gonorrhoeae, chlamydia negative; cervical culture grew N. gonorrhoeae susceptible to ceftriaxone and cefixime. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily; afebrile by hospital day 2, knee swelling improved, ambulating without assistance.

Discharge medications: cefixime 400 mg PO BID to complete 7 days (through 5/8).
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week. Abstain until treatment complete; partner services contacted.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT

Admitted 5/2-5/5 for a third DGI episode, right knee. She brought her discharge instructions; full records requested. Per her paperwork: knee tapped in the ED, the Gram stain was negative, cultures sent; cervical swab positive for gonorrhea; IV ceftriaxone then cefixime. Last cefixime dose tonight.

Today: no fever since Monday. Knee swelling down; still sore at the end of the day. Palm spots gone.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Right knee: mild residual swelling, no redness, flexion slightly limited. Palms clear. Other joints normal.

A/P
1. Disseminated gonococcal infection, third episode, finishing oral step-down today. Return for fever or worsening knee. I'll check in by portal in a couple of weeks.
2. High-risk sexual behavior. Condoms with each partner; partner treatment again.
